chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, from Aslam, from his father, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and every intoxicant is wine.'

key_terms.خَمْرٌ: Wine; used here as a generic term for all intoxicants
key_terms.مُسْكِرٍ: Intoxicant; a substance that causes intoxication

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on all intoxicants in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Baqir (AS), establishes the 'illah (effective cause) of intoxication as the basis for the prohibition of all intoxicants, a principle central to Shia usul al-fiqh. By equating every muskir with khamr, it extends the Quranic ruling on wine to include all substances causing intoxication, regardless of their source or name. This foundational text supports the consensus (ijma) among Shia jurists on the impurity and prohibition of all intoxicants.
